title: The Personalization Trap: How User Memory Alters Emotional Reasoning in LLMs
benchmark_measurement: Bias in emotional understanding and guidance based on user religious identity. The benchmark measured performance differences on emotional intelligence tests when the user profile was associated with Muslim, Christian, or non-religious identities.
findings: Models exhibit demographic biases in emotional understanding based on the user's religion. For instance, DeepSeek R1 performed better with Christian user profiles than with Muslim ones. In contrast, Qwen 3 4B showed better performance for Muslim and non-binary personas compared to other groups. These findings indicate that a user's specified religion can systematically alter an LLM's emotional reasoning capabilities.
